question: Ticket 150133a3ca74 says "When a door refuses to cast a red's ticket (or on StoreUnreachable), run_proof raises an unticketed trouble and either re-raises (door refusal) or continues without writing a ticket (StoreUnreachable)", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.5 reads "Reds don't get lost. Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds and every orphaned file it sees, unless one is already open for it. A red seen in passing gets the same treatment. Every red and every orphaned file is fixed; one unrelated to the work in hand is ticketed, and once it is, that crossing can go ahead." (The outline clause requires 'Each run writes a ticket for every new red it finds...unless one is already open for it.' The ticket proposes that StoreUnreachable keeps its present behavior where the run continues to completion without having written a ticket. This violates the stated requirement that each run writes a ticket for every new red it encounters. For CastRefused this is mitigated because the run re-raises (fails), but for StoreUnreachable the run completes without writing the ticket, which is a direct contradiction.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: The outline stands, and this ticket no longer claims StoreUnreachable. When the checkout has no commons there is no store to write a ticket in; 0da92a7c054a built and PROVED the trouble that keeps that red from being lost. This ticket does not change that path, so it now sits in bounds.out, and the constraint and falsifier clause that only guarded it are dropped (a guard a hollow build passes is no tooth, Law 8). What this ticket builds, a door refusal, fails the run loud and tries the ticket again on every later run.
